title: Neuhaus Rolls Out the Hummingbird Titanium Core 32er (and 29er)
content:
Neuhaus Metalworks just launched two options for its Hummingbird Core line of titanium frames ($2,999). Made in Taiwan, the nimble and snappy Hummingbird comes in a ready-to-order package in either 29er or 32er with an X-Fusion fork…

29er Hummingbird Ti, left, 32er, right

When Neuhaus first started experimenting with 32in wheels – remember the article Daniel Yang wrote for us? – the two-person bike team were shocked by how much ground they could cover. Nick Neuhaus and Daniel Yang dreamed up a titanium version: lighter and a little stiffer, it would be a rocket ship.

That said, 32ers ain’t for everyone, especially if it doesn’t fit you. Plenty of riders also want an intuitive, familiar feel, which is why the (29) Hummingbird is so popular in the first place. Fit is the very first thing we focus on when Neuhaus designs a bike, so the team split the size range by wheel size, with an overlap at ML. If you’re XL, you should really try the 32er.

Hummingbird Ti29 is the bike that likes to be pushed: a 120 mm fork, 29in wheels, a 66° head angle and 430 mm chainstays. Those are the same numbers that made the steel Hummingbird what it is.

Hummingbird Ti32 is for big days out and covering a lot of ground. Some people call that XC; reasonable people call it “riding our bikes.” It has a 100–110 mm fork, 32er wheels, a 66.5° head angle, and 445 mm chainstays. The big wheels roll over everything and hold their momentum. You could race XC on it, but Neuhaus drew it for exploring.

Check out an informative post on the Neuhaus blog about why they made it and who built these frames, as well as some demystification of the material itself. As for inventory, Neuhaus has frames in stock and shipping today. No pre-orders, no lengthy wait times. Shipping today.
